==Problem==
How many digits are in the base-ten representation of <imath>8^5 \cdot 5^{10} \cdot 15^5</imath>?

<imath>\textbf{(A) } 14 \qquad\textbf{(B) }15 \qquad\textbf{(C) }16 \qquad\textbf{(D) }17 \qquad\textbf{(E) } 18</imath>

==Solution 1==
Prime factorizing this gives us <imath>2^{15}\cdot3^{5}\cdot5^{15}=10^{15}\cdot3^5=243\cdot10^{15}</imath>.

<imath>10^{15}</imath> has <imath>16</imath> digits and <imath>243</imath> = <imath>2.43*10^{2}</imath> gives us <imath>3</imath> more digits. <imath>16+2=\text{\boxed{\textbf{(E) }18}}</imath>

<imath>2.43*10^{17}</imath> has <imath>18</imath> digits

~zhenghua

==Solution 2 (Only if you don't know how to do the rest of the problems and have about 20 minutes left, IT IS NOT recommended)==
Multiplying it out, we get that <imath>8^5 \cdot 5^{10} \cdot 15^5 = 243000000000000000</imath>. Counting, we have the answer is <imath>\text{\boxed{\textbf{(E) }18}}</imath>
~andliu766

==Solution 3 (Similar to Solution 1)==
All the exponents have a common factor of <imath>5</imath> which we can factor out. This leaves us with <imath>(8 \cdot 5^2 \cdot 15)^5 = (3000)^5 = (3 \cdot 1000)^5</imath>. We can then distribute the power leaving us with <imath>3^5 \cdot 10^{3 \cdot 5} = 243 \cdot 10^{15}</imath>. This would be <imath>243</imath> followed by <imath>15</imath> zeros resulting in our answer being <imath>15+3=\text{\boxed{\textbf{(E)}18}}</imath>
~leon_0iler

==Solution 4 (log's) == 
We have 8^5, 5^10, and 15^5, if we do a logarithm base of 10 we can figure out how many digits are in the expression when multiplied. So we have <imath>( (log (5^10 \cdot 8^5 \cdot 15^5))</imath> which using some rules we have <imath>((10log(5))+(5log(8))+(5log(15)))</imath>, using the fact that <imath>log(5)=0.7, log(8)=0.9, log(15)=1.2, </imath> multiplying it out we get <imath>10*0.7+5*0.9+1.2*5</imath>, and since log(1)=0, as this is false as 1 is a digit and not 0, we add one and then take the floor to get us <imath>\text{\boxed{\textbf{(E)}18}}</imath>
~~ Randomuser456
